title: Estimating Rare Events in Language Models with Proper Evaluation
abstract: arXiv:2607.18454v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Quantifying the risk of rare failures in language models, such as those triggered by adversarial distribution shifts or very large-scale deployments, requires estimating probabilities far too small for random sampling. While recent work has formalized low-probability estimation, existing pipelines remain fragile in the rarest regimes: standard evaluation losses can become unstable or poorly matched to asymmetric safety costs, and estimators can suffer zero-estimate collapse or systematic bias. In this work, we introduce the Shifted-Power Bregman (SPB) Loss, a proper scoring rule that remains finite for zero-estimates and offers tunable asymmetry between underestimation and overestimation penalties, making all estimators, including those whose estimates collapse to zero, comparable under an explicit cost profile. translated_title: 基于恰当评估的语言模型稀有事件估计
translated_abstract: 量化语言模型中稀有失败的风险，例如由对抗性分布偏移或超大规模部署所引发的失败，需要估计远超随机采样能力范围的极小概率。尽管近期研究已将低概率估计问题形式化，但现有流程在最稀有的情形下仍然脆弱：标准评估损失可能变得不稳定，或与不对称的安全成本不匹配，且估计器可能出现零估计坍缩或系统性偏差。在本工作中，我们提出了移位幂Bregman（SPB）损失，这是一种恰当评分规则，在零估计时仍保持有限值，并在低估与高估惩罚之间提供可调节的不对称性，使得所有估计器——包括估计坍缩为零的估计器——都能在明确的成本配置下进行比较。我们还提出了梯度激活自适应多层分裂（GA-AMLS），该方法改编了稀有事件蒙特卡洛方法……
tldr: 该论文提出移位幂Bregman（SPB）损失和梯度激活自适应多层分裂（GA-AMLS），前者是零估计下仍保持有限且惩罚不对称性可调的恰当评分规则，后者是自适应的稀有事件蒙特卡洛方法，二者共同解决了语言模型极小概率风险估计中评估损失不稳定与估计器零坍缩、系统性偏差的问题。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces the Shifted-Power Bregman (SPB) Loss, a proper scoring rule that remains finite at zero estimates with tunable asymmetric penalties, and Gradient Activation Adaptive Multilevel Splitting (GA-AMLS), jointly addressing instability, zero-estimate collapse, and systematic bias in rare-event probability estimation for language models.
